artists.biography:
The Levellers are an English rock band influenced by punk and traditional English music. They are based in Brighton, England where they were founded in 1988. There are several stories regarding how they got their name; from the Levellers, a radically democratic faction of Oliver Cromwell's New Model Army; as a reference to "The Level", a flat open space near where members of the band used to live in Brighton; or simply, according to guitarist, Simon Friend, a word they chose from a dictionary. Strongly interested and outspoken about green anarchism issues the band have built up a strong and devoted fanbase, despite being nearly universally ignored by mainstream critics. The band have been spokespeople for a number of issues including campaigning against the Criminal Justice Act (and its measures against rave parties ) and various anti-capitalist and environmental issues. They continue to tour extensively around Britain and Europe but maintain a mutual dislike with the music press which stems from their early days.

It is a little known fact that The Levellers had more gold and platinum selling albums in the 1990s than any other UK band in that decade.

perplexity.description:
A Weapon Called the Word is the debut album by English folk rock band the Levellers, released in 1990. Recorded live in a single session at Loco Studios in Wales with producer Phil Tennant, the album blends alternative pop/rock with Celtic rock influences, establishing the band's signature sound that would define their career. The recording process was notably turbulent, with the band members unfamiliar with studio work and tensions arising between the band and producer, yet they managed to complete the album on schedule despite these challenges.

The album features several of the Levellers' most enduring songs, including "Carry Me," "England My Home," and "World Freakshow," which would become fan favorites for decades to come. The 12-track collection showcases the band's folk-inflected rock approach, with a total runtime of approximately 43 minutes. Despite its later recognition, the album achieved BPI Gold certification without charting commercially at the time of its initial release.

More than three decades after its release, A Weapon Called the Word remains a fan favorite and a cornerstone of the Levellers' discography. The album's raw, live-recorded aesthetic and socially conscious songwriting established the template for the band's subsequent work and helped define the British folk-rock revival of the early 1990s.
